sections.html:
Value questions go to the Tax Office at 13 Abbitt Street in Roxboro. Mail goes to the Tax Assessor, PO Box 1116, Roxboro, NC 27573, and the phone number is (336) 597-1721.

Each year the commissioners set a rate once the budget is finalized in June. They pick it to raise the yield the budget needs for services such as law enforcement, solid waste, emergency services, elections, the library, health and social programs, recreation and agricultural extension.

  • Email for informal appeals: tax@personcountync.gov, the county's preferred route.
  • Mail: Person County Tax Assessor, PO Box 1116.
  • In person: the Abbitt Street office.

Before you list, the same office can tell you the value on the record and whether a relief program touches the parcel.

sections.h2: Person County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The county has 19,023 housing units and 16,063 households, with about 40,636 residents, up 4.0% from the 2020 base. Owners live in 77.3% of homes, and the typical owner-occupied house is worth $213,900. Median household income is $63,300.

Those are countywide estimates and say nothing about any one parcel. Your own assessed value on the county record is what the tax bill uses.

Values were last reset as of January 1, 2025. Owners who disagreed with a notice of value had a short window that has since closed, so the route now is the informal review described below.

The county builds a number from comparable local sales, the cost to rebuild, potential income, location, property type, and the age, size, quality, condition and style of the improvements. An owner who finds the number fair does not need to do anything.

The state requires a reappraisal at least once every eight years, and a county may choose a shorter cycle (G.S. 105-286). The 2025 schedule of values stays in force until the next one, so ask the office when that will be. The property record card shows how a given house was priced.

An informal appeal goes to the Assessor's office on the form attached to your value notice. County appraisers handle it without a board hearing, and the county says most owners start here.

Reviewers may recheck year built, square footage, bathrooms and other features. Put a daytime phone number on the form and attach every document you want considered. The county will not open the file until the completed form arrives.

The Assessor writes back to report any change. Filing informally leaves your right to a formal appeal intact, and you can decide after reading the reply.

The formal path goes through the county equalization board. Its first session opens in the window running from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in May, and it takes requests until it adjourns (G.S. 105-322). A further appeal to the state commission is due 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290). Ask the office for this year's meeting dates.

sections.h2: Homestead relief for Person County owners
sections.html:
Three state programs cover a primary residence only. Applications are due June 1, and the income figures below are the 2026 ones.

Person County homestead relief, 2026
ProgramMain terms
Elderly or disabled exclusionIncome $38,800 or below; 65 or totally and permanently disabled before January 1; reduction of $25,000 or 50% of value, whichever is greater, on the home and one acre
Disabled veteran exclusionHonorably discharged and 100% disabled from a service injury; $45,000 off the value of the home and one acre
Circuit breaker65 or disabled; five years of ownership and occupancy; income up to $58,200; tax limited to 4% of income at $38,800 or less, 5% above that; annual application

The circuit breaker defers the excess tax as a lien. If the owner dies, the property transfers, or it stops being a permanent residence, the last three years of deferred tax come due with interest. When several owners hold title, all must apply and qualify, though a married couple holding as tenants by the entirety does not count as multiple owners.

The county also runs a land use and deferral program for farm and forest land. If eligibility ends, deferred taxes become due for the current year plus three prior years. Homestead applications are available from the Tax Office.

One statewide calendar applies. Tax is due September 1 and can be paid at face value through January 5. Interest begins January 6 (G.S. 105-360). The first charge is 2%, and from February 1 it runs three-quarters of 1% for each month or fraction.

  • Personal property listing runs through January 31.
  • A good-cause extension for an individual cannot go past April 15.
  • A mailed payment counts on its postmark date.

Ask the Person County Tax Office for its bill mailing date, payment methods and any prepayment discount for the year you are selling.

sections.h2: How a Roxboro-area sale treats the tax bill
sections.html:
The lien for each year attaches as of the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs join it (G.S. 105-355). A buyer inherits unpaid tax unless closing clears it.

So the closing attorney asks the office for a payoff. If the current year is not yet billed, the parties usually agree on a split. Tax left unpaid can lead to a foreclosure suit, a courthouse-door auction and a right to redeem before confirmation (G.S. 105-374).

  • Request a balance for each parcel, farmland included.
  • Ask about deferrals tied to relief or use-value programs.
  • File the paid receipts with your closing papers.

A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval, but the tax payoff is still taken from your proceeds at the table.

sections.h2: Questions for the Roxboro tax office before listing
sections.html:
A short call can prevent a delay at closing. Write down the answers and give them to your closing attorney.

  • What is the assessed value on the record, and does the record match the house today, including any addition or demolished outbuilding?
  • Is there any balance, interest or prior-year bill on the parcel?
  • Was an informal appeal still open when the last notice was mailed?
  • Does the property carry an elderly, disabled, veteran or circuit breaker benefit, and will the sale end it?
  • Are deferred taxes recorded against the land?

Ask the office how a change of owner affects any benefit, and remember the June 1 filing date for relief applications.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Person County informal appeal?
faqs.a: Email tax@personcountync.gov, mail it to PO Box 1116, Roxboro, NC 27573, or drop it at 13 Abbitt Street. Include your phone number and supporting records.

faqs.q: What value date did the latest reappraisal use?
faqs.a: January 1, 2025. Ask the office when the next one is scheduled.

faqs.q: What income ceiling applies to the elderly exclusion?
faqs.a: $38,800 for 2026, and owners must be 65 or totally and permanently disabled before January 1. Filing closes June 1.

faqs.q: How large is the disabled veteran exclusion?
faqs.a: It removes $45,000 from the value of the home and one acre for an honorably discharged veteran who is 100% disabled by a service injury.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the January 5 deadline?
faqs.a: Interest starts January 6 at 2%, then three-quarters of 1% monthly. Continued nonpayment lets the county enforce its lien through court, so call early.
